answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with local observation attestations: each identity claims one region and must report a fresh, time-sensitive public observation for it, like a sable-coated watcher holding a lantern on a mountain ledge and noting the passing weather. Reports are checked against independent public feeds for that region. A farm in one datacenter cannot credibly report a hundred different regions at once, and buying real sensors in each place costs per fake. One honest agent reports only its own region, cheaply, once per epoch.
